audit_items.state_context: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN = b'RCKZGCBATCH__V1_' (16 bytes, Fulu fork constant in c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1). RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_BATCH_DOMAIN = b'RCKZGBATCH___V1_' (16 bytes, Deneb fork constant). These differ at byte positions 5-9 (C vs space). Domain separator is a compiled constant in the C library, not accessible or configurable at the Go layer.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN = b'RCKZGCBATCH__V1_' (Fulu) is structurally distinct from RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_BATCH_DOMAIN = b'RCKZGBATCH___V1_' (Deneb) and all other KZG domain separators in c-kzg-4844. The Go layer (kzg.go) is a pure type-conversion wrapper — domain logic lives entirely in the C library. The Fiat-Shamir challenge is computed by SHA-256 over: domain (16 bytes) || FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (8 bytes) || num_commitments (8 bytes) || num_cells (8 bytes) || all commitments || all commitment_indices || all cell_indices || all cells || all proofs. No cross-protocol domain collision is possible with existing Ethereum domains since the strings are lexicographically distinct and neither is a prefix of the other.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Domain separator is a static compile-time constant in the C library. No runtime derivation or caching.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrency issue. The constant is read-only.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Attack scenario: an attacker uses a valid Deneb blob proof (domain RCKZGBATCH___V1_) against the Fulu cell batch verifier (RCKZGCBATCH__V1_). This requires a SHA-256 collision between the two distinct domain-prefixed hash inputs, which is computationally infeasible (2^128 security). No cross-protocol replay vector identified. The pairing check embedded in c-kzg-4844 additionally requires the proof to satisfy the correct polynomial evaluation at the cell's evaluation point — a second independent cryptographic barrier.
attack_scenarios: Cross-protocol proof replay (Deneb blob proof → Fulu cell verifier): blocked by domain separator difference causing SHA-256 challenge mismatch
Domain prefix collision search: SHA-256 collision hardness (2^128) makes this infeasible

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The domain separator is a compiled-in C constant, not reachable or modifiable from external input. Cross-protocol replay requires crafting a cryptographic preimage, which is computationally infeasible.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker can supply proof bytes, but the domain separator is applied internally by c-kzg-4844 before verification. No bypass of domain application exists.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN is globally unique and collision-free. Proof: (1) Lexicographic comparison with all c-kzg-4844 domains shows no equality. (2) Neither string is a prefix of the other. (3) SHA-256 provides 128-bit collision resistance. (4) Runtime assert in C library enforces DOMAIN_STR_LENGTH == 16. The invariant holds.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: c-kzg-4844 static domain constant + SHA-256 collision resistance
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. Two independent cryptographic barriers (domain hash + pairing check) prevent cross-protocol replay.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN is globally unique, collision-free, and correctly applied by the c-kzg-4844 library for all verification invocations. No cross-protocol replay attack is feasible.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No change needed. The domain separator design is sound.

audit_items.state_context: The kzgVerifierRoutine drains the kzgChan and batches all pending requests into one batch (verifyKzgBatch). If any column in the batch has an invalid KZG proof, ALL verifiers in that batch receive the same error. The fallback path (validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs per-requester) is triggered, which re-verifies each requester's columns individually. Foreign-domain proof rejection is enforced at the cryptographic level by c-kzg-4844, not at the Go application layer.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: P2P gossip validation does not implement explicit domain-separator checking at the Go layer — rejection of foreign-domain proofs relies entirely on cryptographic failure from c-kzg-4844. The batch architecture in verifyKzgBatch has a contamination property: one invalid column causes ALL concurrently batched verifiers to receive an error (even if their individual columns are valid), triggering fallback unbatched verification for all. This is a performance issue under adversarial conditions but NOT a security bypass — the fallback correctly re-verifies each set independently and rejects invalid columns.
state_anomalies_found: Batch contamination: In verifyKzgBatch, a single invalid column causes ALL batched verifiers to receive verificationErr. Peers with valid columns are forced into the fallback path. Under sustained adversarial column submission, this could degrade P2P performance significantly.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No caching of KZG results at this level. Each gossip message triggers a fresh verification.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: kzgVerifierRoutine uses a non-blocking inner loop (default case) to drain the kzgChan before calling verifyKzgBatch. This is safe but means batch size is non-deterministic and depends on goroutine scheduling.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Security path: attacker submits a DataColumnSidecar with a proof computed under a foreign domain (e.g., RCKZGBATCH___V1_). The proof bytes are structurally valid (48 bytes) so format checks pass. VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch which calls ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. The C library applies RCKZGCBATCH__V1_ internally, computes the Fiat-Shamir challenge, and performs the pairing check. A foreign-domain proof will fail the pairing check → returns false → ErrInvalidKZGProof → ValidationReject. No bypass path found. Performance concern: batch contamination forces fallback verification for all co-batched peers.
attack_scenarios: Foreign-domain proof injection: cryptographically rejected by c-kzg-4844 pairing check. No bypass.

Batch contamination DoS: attacker sends continuous invalid columns to force all P2P peers into fallback verification path, degrading throughput. This is a performance degradation, not a security bypass.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Batch size depends on goroutine scheduling. Under high load, larger batches increase contamination radius.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: P2P gossip rejection of foreign-domain proofs is guaranteed by the cryptographic failure at c-kzg-4844. The batch contamination DoS is externally reachable (attacker can submit malformed columns) but only affects performance, not security.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker can submit invalid-proof columns triggering batch contamination. The ValidationReject result is correctly applied to the invalid sender. The performance degradation affects the verification queue but does not allow invalid proofs to pass.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: foreign-domain proofs are rejected at the P2P layer. This invariant holds because: (1) all verification paths call ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch which applies RCKZGCBATCH__V1_; (2) the pairing check enforces proof validity under this domain; (3) the fallback path correctly re-verifies each requester individually. The batch contamination is a liveness concern (throughput), not a safety concern (correct rejection).
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: c-kzg-4844 pairing check with RCKZGCBATCH__V1_ domain + fallback individual verification path
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for security. Batch contamination DoS is a known design tradeoff in batch verification architectures.
edge_cases: Under sustained adversarial column spam, the fallback path could be continuously triggered, effectively disabling batch efficiency for all peers in the same verifier routine

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Foreign-domain proofs are correctly rejected at the cryptographic level. The batch contamination is a performance concern (DoS amplification), not a security vulnerability since the fallback path correctly handles individual verification. DoS-only issues typically require demonstration of severe impact beyond normal P2P spam handling.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Consider per-requester error isolation in verifyKzgBatch: record individual verification errors per kzgVerifier rather than broadcasting a shared error. This would prevent contamination of valid peers by a single malicious one.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm uses a single verification function (VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs or VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData) for all cell KZG proof verification. The domain separator is not configurable at the Go layer — it is hardcoded in c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1. No legacy or fallback verification modes were found that use a different domain.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: All validator KZG cell proof verification flows through a single code path converging on ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch with the Fulu domain RCKZGCBATCH__V1_. Three distinct entry points were identified: P2P gossip handling, RPC block submission handler, and the internal verification package. All three use the same kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch wrapper which delegates to c-kzg-4844. No code path using a different domain separator or legacy verification mode was found.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No domain-sensitive caching. Each verification call is fresh.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Domain is a static constant. No concurrency issue.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Searched for all usages of VerifyCellKZGProofBatch and VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData in the codebase. All paths terminate at ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. No alternative verification path using a different domain was found. The domain separator is not configurable via config params (params.BeaconConfig() does not expose a KZG domain setting).
attack_scenarios: Dual-verification path with different domains: not present in codebase
Domain override via configuration: not possible — domain is in C library constant

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The domain separator is uniformly applied across all validator verification paths. No attacker-accessible path to use a different domain was identified.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. Domain is a C library constant.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: all validators use identical domain separator RCKZGCBATCH__V1_, hardcoded and not configurable. Proof: (1) single Go wrapper function kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch; (2) c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1 has static domain constant; (3) no alternative KZG cell verification function was found; (4) domain not exposed in BeaconConfig. The invariant holds.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Single c-kzg-4844 library with hardcoded domain, used by all verification paths
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. Single code path eliminates risk of domain divergence between validators.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: All validator KZG cell proof verification uses identical domain separator through all code paths. Domain is hardcoded in c-kzg-4844, not configurable. No domain divergence risk exists.

audit_items.state_context: The domain separator is a static C string literal in c-kzg-4844 library (v2.1.1). It is NOT derived from a hash — it IS the domain separator input to the SHA-256 hash. The Fiat-Shamir challenge r is computed as SHA-256(domain || FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL || num_commitments || num_cells || all_commitments || all_commitment_indices || all_cell_indices || all_cells || all_proofs). Runtime C asserts verify strlen(domain) == DOMAIN_STR_LENGTH and offset == bytes + input_size.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: RCKZGCBATCH__V1_ is a 16-byte ASCII static constant, not derived from a hash. It serves as the domain prefix for the SHA-256 Fiat-Shamir challenge computation. The question of 'collision-resistant derivation' does not apply — the domain IS the prefix, and the challenge is collision-resistant by virtue of SHA-256. Analysis: (1) 16-byte string with sufficient entropy for a domain separator; (2) distinct from RCKZGBATCH___V1_ (differ at positions 5-9); (3) SHA-256 provides 128-bit collision resistance; (4) fixed-size hash input prevents length-extension attacks; (5) C runtime asserts enforce correctness.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Three attack scenarios evaluated: (1) Prefix collision between RCKZGCBATCH__V1_ and RCKZGBATCH___V1_ — not applicable since they differ structurally and SHA-256 collision resistance prevents crafting equivalent-hash inputs. (2) Length extension: SHA-256 uses fixed-size input buffer (input_size is computed before SHA-256 call), not susceptible to Merkle-Damgård length extension. (3) Low-entropy domain enabling collision search: domain is 16 bytes of ASCII — 2^128 space is computationally infeasible to search. No attack vector found.
attack_scenarios: Prefix collision: not applicable — domains are lexicographically distinct and SHA-256 collision resistance applies
Length extension attack: prevented by fixed-size buffer approach in c-kzg-4844
Collision search on domain entropy: 2^128 space (SHA-256 strength) — computationally infeasible

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Domain separator is a compiled constant unreachable from external input. All attack scenarios require breaking SHA-256 collision resistance.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: RCKZGCBATCH__V1_ is a collision-resistant domain separator. Proof: (1) It is a well-defined 16-byte constant with documented purpose (Fulu KZG cell batch domain); (2) It is structurally unique among all c-kzg-4844 domains; (3) SHA-256 provides 128-bit collision resistance making hash-based collision infeasible; (4) Fixed-size input prevents length-extension attacks; (5) Runtime C asserts enforce string length (== 16) and full buffer utilization. The invariant holds.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SHA-256 with 128-bit collision resistance + static 16-byte domain constant + C runtime asserts
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. No practical cryptographic attack exists against this design.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The domain separator is a well-constructed 16-byte constant used correctly as the SHA-256 hash prefix in a deterministic Fiat-Shamir challenge. It is collision-resistant, unique among all Ethereum KZG domains, and correctly implemented with runtime safety assertions in c-kzg-4844.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No change needed. Domain separator design is sound.

audit_items.state_context: Each DataColumnSidecar carries data for one column (sidecar.Index = column index 0-127) across all blobs in a block. For a block with N blobs, one sidecar with index=k contains N cells (one per blob), N commitments, and N proofs. In VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs, indices is populated with sidecar.Index repeated N times for each sidecar. The c-kzg-4844 cell_indices parameter represents the column index in the EIP-7594 erasure coding scheme (0-127), not a row index. The Fiat-Shamir challenge r = SHA-256(domain || ... || all cell_indices || ... || all cells || all proofs) is computed from the presented order of inputs.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Hash input ordering in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs is determined by: (1) outer loop over sidecars slice (sidecar arrival order), (2) inner loop over sidecar.Column by index i (deterministic per-sidecar). The indices array uses sidecar.Index (column number), which is correct per EIP-7594 — each cell in a DataColumnSidecar belongs to the same column. The ordering is deterministic within a single function call, but may vary across calls due to batch merging in verifyKzgBatch (arrival-order-dependent). The Fiat-Shamir challenge is freshly computed for each call, so inter-call ordering variation is safe.
state_anomalies_found: In verifyKzgBatch (batch_verifier.go), multiple kzgVerifier requests are merged into allDataColumns in channel arrival order (non-deterministic under concurrent load). However, the challenge r is freshly computed from the presented order each time, making this safe from a cryptographic standpoint.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No caching of hash inputs or challenges. Each call computes fresh challenge r.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: kzgVerifierRoutine processes one batch at a time via a non-blocking inner loop drain pattern. The batch assembly is single-threaded within the goroutine.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Attack scenario: attacker sends sidecars in different orders to different nodes, hoping that some ordering allows an invalid proof to pass. Analysis: the Fiat-Shamir challenge r = SHA-256(all inputs including cell bytes) is computed fresh per call. Reordering changes r but does NOT relax the pairing constraint for any individual (commitment_i, cell_index_i, cell_i, proof_i) tuple. The batch pairing check in c-kzg-4844 verifies a random linear combination of individual claims — each claim must be valid for its own (commitment, cell_index, cell). Swapping proof_j to position k requires proof_j to satisfy polynomial f_k at evaluation point ω^{cell_index_k}, which it does not (unless f_j = f_k at that point). No ordering-based bypass found.
attack_scenarios: Order manipulation to bypass pairing check: infeasible — each cell's pairing equation must hold independently regardless of ordering

Different orderings producing different challenges causing cross-node disagreement: each node computes fresh challenge from its own input order; all nodes with same inputs produce same result (verification is locally consistent)
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Batch merging ordering depends on goroutine scheduling — benign for cryptographic correctness.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The hash input ordering is determined by the sidecar iteration order of the input slice. Attackers can control sidecar content (cells, proofs) but not the verification function's iteration logic. The non-determinism in batch merging is an internal implementation detail not exploitable by external attackers.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Content-based attacks (invalid cells/proofs) are rejected by the pairing check. No ordering-based attack vector exists.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: hash input ordering is deterministic and canonical for each verification call. Proof: (1) Within VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs, ordering is deterministic (Go slice iteration order is well-defined); (2) The indices use sidecar.Index (column number 0-127), which is the correct EIP-7594 cell index parameter; (3) Commitments, cells, and proofs are aligned (all 4 arrays appended in the same inner loop iteration, maintaining correspondence); (4) Non-determinism across batch-merged calls does not violate the invariant because each call computes its own fresh challenge. The invariant holds within the scope of a single verification invocation.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Deterministic Go slice iteration + fresh Fiat-Shamir challenge per call + per-cell pairing check binding
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. The invariant 'same inputs → same result' holds. Non-determinism of batch merging ordering is harmless.
edge_cases: When verifyKzgBatch merges multiple kzgVerifier requests in arrival order, the cell ordering within the merged batch is non-deterministic across different runs. This is safe for verification correctness but means the combined batch's internal ordering is not canonically defined across nodes (since different nodes may batch differently). Each node's verification is internally consistent.
Empty sidecar.Column case: if a sidecar has 0 cells, the inner loop produces no appends — correct behavior, no panic risk.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Hash input ordering is deterministic within each verification call and correct relative to EIP-7594 (sidecar.Index is the proper column index for cell_indices). Non-determinism across batch-merged calls is a known and cryptographically safe property — each verification is locally consistent. No ordering-based bypass of proof verification exists.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Document that cell ordering within a batch verification call does not need to match any canonical cross-node order, since the Fiat-Shamir challenge handles arbitrary ordering correctly. Consider adding a comment in verifyKzgBatch noting that the merged ordering is arrival-dependent but cryptographically safe.
